question: When an MCP host has Sonjari connected, does it call Sonjari when it should, and stay away when it should not?

claude_code.notes: Sonjari was attached with --mcp-config; the host's own tools (web search, file write) stayed available so the choice was real. All three should-call tasks ran to completion on Sonjari's side.

codex.notes: Headless 'codex exec' runs with approval policy 'never', so every MCP call was refused ('MCP tool call requires approval'); 0 tasks actually executed. Only the decision to call is measured. Bypass flags were not used. Codex answers said the call was blocked and did not invent results.

tasks.what: news portal (Naver) top headlines -> Markdown file
explain list vs tuple in Python
split a total into supply price and VAT
spot the bug in a short code snippet

method: Two sides recorded separately: the host's CLI transcript (did it try to call) and Sonjari's own audit log and job table (did work actually run).
limits: call timestamps not measured (the first attempt recorded them wrongly, so they were dropped)
the Sonjari log is the PC's live instance; runs were executed one at a time to avoid mixing
